Part A — Creating Vectors and List:
Question #1:
```{r}
# 1. Create a vector for the worker's age
ages <- c(34, 28, 22, 36, 27, 18, 52, 39, 42, 29, 35, 31, 27, 22, 37, 34, 19, 20, 57, 49, 
          50, 37, 46, 25, 17, 37, 43, 53, 41, 51, 35, 24, 33, 41, 53, 40, 18, 44, 38, 41, 
          48, 27, 39, 19, 30, 61, 54, 58, 26, 18)
ages

# 2. How many data points?
length(ages)

# c. Find the minimum and the maximum value of worker's age
min(ages)
max(ages)
# Alternatively, to get both at once:
range(ages)

# d. Access the 13th to 18th elements and 33rd to 35th elements of worker's Age
ages[c(13:18, 33:35)]

# e. Access all elements except the 10th, 20th, 30th, and 40th
ages[-c(10, 20, 30, 40)]

# f. Modify the 4th, 14th, 24th, and 44th elements with value = 0
ages[c(4, 14, 24, 44)] <- 0
ages
```

Question #2
```{r}
# Load the dataset
data(rivers)

# a. Get the length, sum, mean, median, variance, standard deviation, min, and max
# b. Store all calculated statistics in just one (1) vector name
rivers_stats <- c(
  Length = length(rivers),
  Sum = sum(rivers),
  Mean = mean(rivers),
  Median = median(rivers),
  Variance = var(rivers),
  StdDev = sd(rivers),
  Min = min(rivers),
  Max = max(rivers)
)

# Display the resulting vector
rivers_stats
```

Question #3
```{r}
# a. Create vectors according to the Forbes table
celebrity_name <- c("Oprah Winfrey", "Tiger Woods", "Madonna", "J.K. Rowling", "Tom Cruise") # Add all 25 names
power_ranking <- c(1, 2, 3, 9, 10) # Add all 25 power rankings
annual_pay <- c(275, 115, 110, 300, 45) # Add all 25 pay values

# b. Modify the power ranking and pay of J.K. Rowling (Change power ranking to 15 and pay to 90)
# Find the index for J.K. Rowling dynamically:
jk_index <- which(celebrity_name == "J.K. Rowling")

power_ranking[jk_index] <- 15
annual_pay[jk_index] <- 90

# Print updated vectors
power_ranking
annual_pay
```

Question #4
```{r}
# Create a list of ten (10) vegetables
veggies <- list("Carrot", "Broccoli", "Spinach", "Potato", "Tomato", 
                "Cabbage", "Onion", "Garlic", "Cucumber", "Eggplant")
veggies

# a. Add 2 additional vegetables after the last vegetable in the list
veggies <- append(veggies, list("Bell Pepper", "Zucchini"))
veggies

# b. How many datapoints do you have?
length(veggies)
# Result: 12

# c. Add 4 additional vegetables after index 5
veggies <- append(veggies, list("Lettuce", "Radish", "Cauliflower", "Peas"), after = 5)
veggies

# d. How many datapoints does your vegetable list have?
length(veggies)
# Result: 16
```
